subject: Liu et al. (2021)
object: Liu et al. (2021) reported 3 unrelated Chinese men with primary infertility caused by asthenoteratozoospermia characterized by multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella (MMAF), as well as an Australian man with severe asthenoteratozoospermia. The authors stated that all men carrying hemizygous CFAP47 variants had typical MMAF phenotypes.

subject: Liu et al. (2021)
object: In 3 unrelated Chinese men with MMAF, Liu et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing to identify hemizygous missense variants in the X-linked CFAP47 gene. The 3 variants were absent from human control population genome databases and were predicted to be deleterious by multiple bioinformatic tools. Immunoblotting and immunofluorescence showed obviously reduced CFAP47 levels in spermatozoa from all 3 men.

subject: Liu et al. (2021)
object: Using whole-exome sequencing data from an additional cohort of men with severe asthenoteratozoospermia from Australia, Liu et al. (2021) identified a hemizygous deletion at Xp21.1 that removed the entire CFAP47 gene.

subject: CFAP47 hemizygous Xp21.1 deletion removing the entire CFAP47 gene
Liu et al. (2021)
object: Liu et al. (2021) noted that CFAP47 encodes a cilia- and flagella-associated protein that is highly expressed in testis.

subject: Liu et al. (2021)
object: Liu et al. (2021) generated a Cfap47-mutated mouse model. Adult male mutant mice were sterile and had reduced sperm motility and abnormal flagellar morphology and movement, but fertility could be rescued by intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI).

subject: Liu et al. (2021)
object: Based on findings in humans and mice, Liu et al. (2021) concluded that hemizygous CFAP47 mutations cause X-linked MMAF and asthenoteratozoospermia, and suggested a good prognosis with ICSI.

subject: Liao et al. (2022)
object: Liao et al. (2022) screened 7 men with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF) for gene mutations. In one of them they found two novel variants in the CFAP47 gene: c.706G>A (Val236Met) and c.1337C>T (Thr446Met).

subject: Liao et al. (2022)
object: Liao et al. (2022) found by immunoblotting and immunofluorescence that CFAP47 was dramatically reduced in sperm from the man with the CFAP47 variants. WDR87 expression was also significantly reduced, with weak signals next to the sperm nuclei. The authors concluded that CFAP47 was needed to transport WDR87 during the formation of the sperm flagellum.

subject: Liao et al. (2022)
object: Liao et al. (2022) found that WDR87 was highly expressed in human and mouse testis. In mice it sat in the cytoplasm around the nucleus of spermatocytes and round spermatids, moved to the manchette during spermiogenesis, and ended up in the middle piece of the sperm tail. They identified CFAP47 as a protein that interacts with WDR87 in the sperm flagellar midpiece. They concluded that the two proteins form a complex involved in assembling the sperm tail.
